analysis:
Examined the three base-text units of scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py plus the supplied patch excerpt. This is an offline CI workflow-structure test with no provider runtime code. The patch has two parts. First, it adds an assertion that the tested-tree record step runs `ci-tested-tree.py tree-name` and adds the 'Upload the tree record' step to the skip-condition check. Second, it changes the build-job `if` assertion from `inputs.<lane> == 'true' || (push && skip && changed_<lane>)` to plain `inputs.<lane> == 'true'`, so tested-tree pushes skip the build jobs.

I found no security regression against the threat model. The test is not shipped to providers or the coordinator, and it does not touch the WebSocket boundary (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), key custody (A-002, A-003) or consumer prompt confidentiality (A-001).

The surrounding unchanged tests still enforce the following. Cache saves are limited to master or dev pushes via SAVE_CACHES. There is no `secrets.` reference in the parity job. Checkouts use persist-credentials: false. Git cache validation discards hooks and unsafe config. Strict cache restore applies on master. The prompt-fixture cache is keyed on manifest hashes with no restore-keys.

The T-041 definition concerns the on-disk prefix cache, not CI caches. The patch does not touch any of its affected files.

Residual question for integration: the real workflow and the provider-plan.yml, ci-tested-tree.py and components outputs are not in this batch. Whether skipping the build jobs on tested-tree pushes weakens the supply-chain or cache-refresh guarantees (strict master cache freshness) depends on those files. Whether the new 'tree-name' command and the 'Upload the tree record' step exist in the workflow is also unverified. Those are CI-integrity concerns, not evidenced regressions here. The patch excerpt is truncated, so changes beyond the visible hunks (lines 898-900 base) were not fully seen.
